title: fix: reuse durable generation cache identity
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Reuse the original cache key during background generation, so prompt changes during replay cannot leave callers looking for the wrong file.
- Pass the existing job directly to the executor, removing duplicated argument plumbing.
- Add regression tests for image generations and edits; both fail with the old key calculation.

Validation: 185 tests, TypeScript and Biome pass. Independent Fable review found no blockers.

gist.headline: The cache remembers
gist.blurb: Background image jobs now keep hold of their original cache key, even when a replayed prompt has wandered off to inspect another flower. Image generations and edits can reliably find the pixels they made.
gist.summary: Fixed durable background generation to reuse each job’s original cache key instead of recalculating it from a replayed prompt, with regression coverage for both image generation and image edits.
gist.impact: Users get reliable cached image and edit results: callers now look up the same output file created by the background job even when prompts change during replay.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy garden archive where Polli carefully carries a labeled seed packet—the original cache key—between a retro terminal and a finished pixel-art image plant. The stable label connects the job to its exact output, while a nearby alternate prompt note drifts harmlessly past; use vines and file drawers as a memory/cache metaphor.
gist.image_prompt: Cozy pixel art scene of Polli, a cute bee mascot with a yellow body, dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular cheek blushes, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings, wearing tiny librarian glasses as she carries a glowing original-key seed packet from a retro terminal to its matching blooming image-file plant; a changed prompt note floats safely away, with code-vines and warm file drawers around them. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft lime green (#ecf874) and pastel gradient background, chunky retro sprites, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, with subtle pixel-font text: "SAME KEY".
